Test Description: Testing ability to optimize moves or scoring for a given game state and trying to have a grounded rule application
Difficulty Notes: Easy optimization problem with intuitive solution
Question: Assume: 1) no-inter player trading occurs, 2) there are no development cards left to draw, 3) in-hand VP cards count as points, 4) can use the combined Trade/Build phase, 5)For maritime trade, a city on a special harbor grants a 1:1 trade rate for its resource, while a city on a generic harbor grants a 3:2 trade rate for any resource. 6) consider that the green player in total has 4 cities, 5 settlements (including ones on board). What is the maximum number points the green player has by the end of this turn, given that the green player has rolled 3 in this round? Return your answer in the following format: [prev_points: <number of points before this turn>, new_points: <number of points after the turn>]
Rationale: According to the given board state in the question, the green player has: 1 city at special harbour, and 3 settlements. The current resource pool of the green player is: [brick: 3, wool: 4, grain: 1, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. The development cards include: 1 road building, 1 year of plenty and 1 knight. Also has 3 knights already placed on the table. The total number of points the green player currently has is: 5 points (2 from city + 3 settlements). Since the player rolls a 3 in this turn, the green player gets: 4 grain resources. The resource pool is: [brick: 3, wool: 4, grain: 5, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. The way to get maximum number of settlements + cities is: there are 2 intersections where settlements (cost 1 brick, lumber, wool, grain) can be built: (9) near the special harbor, intersection of (4, 6, desert) -> this gives the player +2 points. Now the maximum number of settlements is completed (5). So now in order to increase the sum, one of the settlement should be upgraded to city (2 grain and 3 ore) -> + 1 point. This results in one settlement return to the players pool. Now using the build road development card, the player can build 2 roads (extending the longest road) -> (3, 11) and (3, 10), getting a maximum road length of 9, and thus the green player gets the longest road (+2 points). This would open up a new place to place another settlement (+1 point). This way the player can place a maximum of 5 settlements and 2 cities by the end of this round. And a total points of 11 points.
